name: udt-authoring: model typed inputs (select + integer)
description: Tier-2 check that UDT authoring models a tool's options as typed inputs rather than baking them into the command. Asks for a seqkit UDT with a sequence-type choice (dna/rna/protein) and a minimum-length number -- which should become a `type: select` with real `options:` and a `type: integer`. Asserts the agent fetched the udt-authoring skill and drafted a GalaxyUserTool declaring both input types plus a populated options block. The three content checks are line-anchored regexes rather than substrings on purpose: `type: select` and `options:` are generic enough that a model merely DESCRIBING the schema in prose ("...one of the options: dna, rna, protein") would satisfy a plain substring without ever writing an inputs block, which is precisely the difference the scenario exists to measure. Requiring each to open a line -- and `options:` to be followed by a list or a flow sequence, not prose -- keeps the check on the YAML. Restricting --tools to skills_fetch forces the agent to draft the YAML in chat so chatText assertions can see it. Mirrors the parameter-shape dimension of Galaxy's custom_tool eval (galaxyproject/galaxy#22968).
inputs: Wrap `seqkit seq` as a Galaxy user-defined tool I can run in my own account. Let the user pick a sequence type -- one of dna, rna, or protein -- and set a minimum sequence length to keep. Draft the full GalaxyUserTool YAML definition; don't create it on the server yet.
